name: Ulster nationalism
summary: Ulster nationalism is a minor current in Northern Ireland politics, arising within unionism, that holds the province's people form their own community entitled to self-rule, either as a dominion or an independent state, rather than being governed from Westminster or absorbed into a united Ireland. Its best-documented programmes pair independence or deep devolution with a written constitution, a bill of rights, a supreme court, proportional representation and coalition power-sharing that includes Catholics. It is culturally Protestant and strongly anti-united-Ireland, and its strongest base was loyalist, including Vanguard and the UDA's research group.
scope: The loyalist-origin strand of the 1970s and 1980s: William Craig's Ulster Vanguard (UDI talk, 1972-74), Glenn Barr, and the UDA's New Ulster Political Research Group (Beyond the Religious Divide, 1979; Common Sense, 1987). Excludes the non-sectarian intellectual variant of Tom Nairn and Liam de Paor, other than where noted, and later fringe groups such as the Ulster Third Way. Most economic and social questions are not addressed by the sources, so many answers are low-confidence inferences.

keyFigures.name: William Craig

keyFigures.name: Glenn Barr
keyFigures.role: Vanguard Assemblyman and UDA leader who called himself an Ulster nationalist.

keyFigures.name: John McMichael
keyFigures.role: UDA commander and secretary of the New Ulster Political Research Group who campaigned on independence.

missingStatements.text: Northern Ireland should be able to leave the United Kingdom without joining the Republic of Ireland.
missingStatements.rationale: The defining aim of the ideology is an independent or dominion Northern Ireland that is neither UK-governed nor part of a united Ireland.

missingStatements.text: A constitutional change should require the approval of two-thirds of voters in a referendum.
missingStatements.rationale: Common Sense says its constitution and any change to Northern Ireland's status need at least two-thirds support in a referendum.
missingStatements.declined: A procedural detail of one party's constitutional draft, not a question other ideologies would take sides on.

missingStatements.text: In a deeply divided society, major communities should share executive power through permanent coalition rather than simple majority rule.
missingStatements.rationale: Common Sense argues majority rule is undemocratic in divided societies and proposes proportional executive posts for all main parties.

notes: The movement is small and split between a loyalist-paramilitary strand (Vanguard, UDA) and a non-sectarian intellectual strand (Nairn, de Paor). Answers follow the loyalist strand's documented constitutional programme. Common Sense and Beyond the Religious Divide are products of the UDA's political arm, so they represent one wing.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Sources are silent on health policy; the loyalist working-class base in Northern Ireland is attached to the UK National Health Service, so support is inferred.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Common Sense names deprivation and unemployment as the real enemies, so a wage floor is inferred as a mild, unstated lean rather than a documented demand.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The sources give almost no economic doctrine; adherents range from Vanguard-style right-wingers to working-class loyalists, so this is left neutral.

public-ownership.rationale: No source states a view on nationalised industry; the only economic stress is on social deprivation, so adherents are treated as split.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Taxation is not discussed in the sources, and the movement mixes labour-leaning loyalists with business-minded unionists.

unions-good.rationale: Barr's account of the 1974 strike shows a movement that organised through trade-union workers in power stations and shipyards, so mild support is inferred.

property-fundamental.rationale: Vanguard was right-wing and unionist, which suggests respect for property, but no source states a doctrine on it.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Economic regulation is not addressed anywhere in the sources reviewed, so no direction can be inferred.

cut-welfare.rationale: Common Sense lists deprivation and housing need as problems to fix after settlement, implying support for welfare rather than cuts.

worker-ownership.rationale: No source supports workplace ownership; the movement's unionist and right-wing roots make it unlikely to back this.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Vanguard demanded the destruction of the IRA and loyalist politics prizes security measures against republican terrorism, so security surveillance is inferred acceptable.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Culturally conservative Protestant loyalism is inferred to oppose legalisation; the sources do not address drugs.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not discussed; a movement defending contested Orange marches as heritage is inferred to resist speech restrictions.

strong-leader.rationale: Common Sense calls Westminster's unchecked sovereignty an elected dictatorship and wants courts and coalition to check power, which cuts against a gridlock-bypassing strongman.

state-harmful.rationale: The movement's whole programme is to build a new state with a written constitution, supreme court and devolved assembly, so a state-less view is flatly rejected.

limit-guns.rationale: Unionist and loyalist politics has valued armed defence of the community; gun control is not addressed, so mild opposition is inferred.

empower-police-military.rationale: Vanguard demanded a hard security response to the Provisional IRA and Barr resented the disarming of the RUC, so more security authority is inferred.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; socially conservative Protestant loyalism is inferred to disapprove.

decide-locally.rationale: The programme is a devolved Ulster assembly deciding everything except defence and foreign affairs, which is a clear preference for decisions nearer home.

rehabilitation.rationale: Vanguard's rhetoric about extermination of the IRA suggests a punitive stance on terrorist crime; no explicit penal doctrine is documented.

traditional-family.rationale: Traditional Ulster nationalism is Protestant-focused and tied to Orange culture, so conservative family views are inferred, not documented.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The Protestant-cultural base is inferred to oppose it, though no source states a position.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from the conservative Protestant base of the movement; the sources are silent on abortion.

more-religion-public.rationale: The article ties Ulster nationalism to the Orange Order and contested marches as heritage, implying an accepted public role for Protestant religion.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Racial injustice in the sense asked is outside the movement's concerns; its own concern is Catholic exclusion, handled through a bill of rights.

gender-social-construct.rationale: No stated view; the culturally conservative base is inferred to reject this.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The movement is built on a distinct Ulster identity and defends Orange parades and Ulster-Scots as cultural heritage.

gradual-change.rationale: Common Sense proposes writing a wholly new constitution and renegotiating the Act of Union, which is not gradualist, though it is non-revolutionary in tone.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigration was not a documented concern of the movement, so it is left neutral.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Barr rejects decisions made behind people's backs by outside actors; international bodies appear only as advisers in Common Sense.

free-trade.rationale: Vanguard backed staying in the EEC, which hints at openness, but no trade doctrine is stated.

nation-first.rationale: Barr says Northern Ireland should put its own interests first, and the independence aim is explicitly about self-rule over outside pressures.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Foreign intervention is far outside the movement's concerns; no inference is possible.

open-borders.rationale: Barr would fight anybody to stay out of a united Ireland and the project is a defended territorial frontier, so open borders are rejected.

limit-growth.rationale: Common Sense wants economic development and jobs; no environmental degrowth theme appears.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate policy is not discussed in any source.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The sources contain no view on technology.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed; no ground for inference.

revolution-justified.rationale: Vanguard and the proposals for a unilateral declaration of independence accepted extra-constitutional resistance if politicians failed, but this was framed defensively.

experts-over-public.rationale: Common Sense insists the constitution be approved by referendum, giving the public the final say, though outside experts may advise the conference.

central-planning.rationale: Right-wing unionist roots make central planning unlikely, though no source addresses it.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Right-leaning unionist base is inferred to dislike it; no document states a position.

basic-income.rationale: Not discussed; Common Sense wants jobs and housing, suggesting a work-based welfare outlook.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Barr's account of the 1974 strike shows concern for Ulster industry and jobs, but no tariff position is stated.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Common Sense lists economic development as an executive department but gives no doctrine on directing investment.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Anti-communist, unionist and right-wing in outlook, so abolishing money and wages is plainly outside the programme.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; monetary orthodoxy is inferred from the unionist base.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Barr's strike coordination of workers and loyalist groups is not the same as a state-recognised bargaining system, so no clear answer.

one-party-rule.rationale: Common Sense rests on proportional representation and permanent coalition of all major parties, and invites British parties to organise locally.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The strand that sought dominion status kept the Crown as head of state, and Ulster identity grew from British loyalty.

democracy-best.rationale: Common Sense calls the only democratic system one with coalition of all groups and demands referenda, endorsing democracy while saying pure majority rule fails in divided societies.

direct-votes.rationale: Common Sense reserves the constitution and its changes to referendum, but not ordinary laws.

workers-councils.rationale: The proposal is a conventional assembly elected by PR, with no place for councils as the basis of power.

right-to-secede.rationale: The movement claims Northern Ireland's right to leave the UK without joining Ireland, though adherents do not extend this as a general principle.

natural-rulers.rationale: Common Sense supports equal participation of all groups and bills of rights, which contradicts inborn fitness to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: Vanguard spoke of liquidating the enemy and the UDA-linked groups used force; most adherents would call defensive violence justified.

separate-church-state.rationale: Adherents tie identity to Protestant culture but the Common Sense constitution is secular in form; the sources show no firm position.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The constitutional model is the US-style written constitution, not scripture, though the base is devout.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Common Sense gives courts and a supreme court to the state and reserves defence to Westminster.

military-superiority.rationale: A defence-minded loyalist movement is inferred to back strong armed forces, but the question is about national rivalry, which sources do not cover.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Beyond the Religious Divide and Nairn and de Paor's version propose a non-sectarian state with power-sharing; though some adherents rely on a separate Ulster ethnic identity.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The movement unites classes in a single Ulster people and is anti-communist in its Vanguard form.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The documents seek equal rights and participation, not equal outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Ulster nationalism rests on a settler-descended Protestant identity and its own claim to the territory, so it would not defer to this principle.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The movement's constituency is descended from Plantation settlers and rejects colonial-guilt claims, though sources are silent.

civilizational-union.rationale: The movement wants a separate Ulster state, not a union of co-religionists.

self-interest-moral.rationale: No source states a moral philosophy of self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Common Sense makes an entrenched bill of rights, with a supreme court able to overrule the assembly, an essential part of the constitution.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed; no support for population control is inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The programme wants development and jobs; there is no sign of primitivist ideas.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The sources never discuss technological change, and a constitutional-reform movement gives no basis for leaning either way.

human-enhancement.rationale: Bodily enhancement is far outside the movement's constitutional concerns, so no direction can be inferred from its documents.

algorithmic-government.rationale: The programme is conventional representative government.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Security-minded, anti-IRA stance suggests state access over private encryption, though not documented.

restore-past-order.rationale: Early Ulster nationalism was a reaction to loss of the Stormont order, but Common Sense and Beyond the Religious Divide propose a new constitution rather than restoration.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Common Sense calls itself common sense and an agreed process, and Barr stresses practical settlements, indicating pragmatism.

direct-action.rationale: Barr describes the 1974 Ulster Workers' Council strike as a successful political lever, and Vanguard held general strikes.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The programme builds a modern state and economy.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Not a stated principle; unionist right-wing base is inferred to oppose it.

production-for-use.rationale: Not stated; inferred from unionist right-wing outlook.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Anti-communist Vanguard and a cross-class Ulster identity reject a theory of exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Vanguard was explicitly anti-communist and the movement seeks a pluralist coalition state.

collective-farming.rationale: Not discussed; incompatible with the movement's right-wing roots.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not stated; anti-communist outlook suggests rejection.

taxation-theft.rationale: Common Sense relies on a functioning state with executive departments, so a theft view is unlikely.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Common Sense stresses group-level safeguards like proportional executive posts and coalition of communities, as well as an individual bill of rights.

conscription.rationale: Hard security outlook suggests acceptance, but there is no stated position.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The programme stresses participation, referenda and elected assemblies as checks.

state-as-business.rationale: Not addressed; the documents see government as a constitutional order.

positive-liberty.rationale: Not addressed beyond naming deprivation as an enemy.

media-academia-power.rationale: Vanguard and the UDA group attacked politicians and Westminster, not universities or the press, so no stance is inferred.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Beyond the Religious Divide proposes a non-sectarian state; no racial theories are documented.

organic-representation.rationale: Proportional party representation is central in Common Sense; Common Sense wants national parties to organise in Ulster.

total-state.rationale: The proposals limit the state by a written constitution, bill of rights and supreme court.

national-rebirth.rationale: Ulster nationalism is a response to perceived decline of the Union but frames itself as new constitutional settlement, not decadence-rebirth.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Independence is defensive; the movement seeks to keep Northern Ireland out of a united Ireland, not to expand.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: A constitution, supreme court and elected assembly are the opposite of rule by oath.

bound-labor.rationale: The state proposed is a modern constitutional democracy with a bill of rights.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Common Sense appeals to reasoned common sense; no relativist theme appears.

universal-morality.rationale: Common Sense proposes to adopt the European Convention on Human Rights or its own bill of rights, hinting at universal rights, but this is inferred.

single-common-good.rationale: Common Sense is built on balancing communities through coalition and proportional power-sharing, not a single common good.

revive-national-language.rationale: The article cites Ulster-Scots support, but not reviving it as the state language.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Strike committees involved workers but no stated view on company governance.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education finance is not covered in Common Sense; Northern Ireland's separate church and state school sectors leave adherents divided.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is never mentioned in the sources, so this is left neutral.

economic-freedom.rationale: Common Sense gives no doctrine linking economic and political freedom, only a call to tackle deprivation after settlement.

rule-by-example.rationale: Common Sense relies on written law, courts and constitutional limits rather than rulers' example.

national-self-determination.rationale: The movement claims that Ulster people may decide their own constitutional future, including independence.

force-without-un.rationale: Foreign military action is outside the movement's concerns; only Vanguard's strong security stance at home is documented.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The movement's culture is Protestant and its documents appeal to common sense, so adherents are split on this contrast.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Migrant access to welfare is not a documented issue for the movement, which concerns two native communities.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Common Sense wants unemployment tackled but sets out no conditions for benefits, so this stays neutral.

class-collaboration.rationale: The movement addresses all Ulster people as a single community in Beyond the Religious Divide and in Common Sense's call for cooperation.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: The movement defends inherited heritage such as Orange parades.

dominated-front.rationale: Not part of the movement's thinking; Barr resents British politicians but does not seek bloc.

workers-nation.rationale: Loyalist workers organised on Ulster lines in 1974; not an international class view.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Inferred from the conservative Protestant base; no documented position.

ban-interest.rationale: No religious ban on interest is part of the programme.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Beyond the Religious Divide proposes bill of rights and power-sharing; race law is outside the programme.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The movement views the state as a neutral constitutional framework.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Energy production policy is absent from the sources apart from Barr's account of power stations during the 1974 strike.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's concerns are about the internal two communities.

elite-replacement.rationale: No source mentions replacement theories; the movement's concerns are internal to Northern Ireland and not migration-driven.

proportional-representation.rationale: Common Sense calls for PR in assembly and council elections and for proportional committees and executive posts.

national-mission.rationale: The programme is inward looking, not missionary.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Barr says he vowed never to trust English politicians and objects to deals done behind people's backs.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not part of the programme; bill of rights approach contradicts.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Vanguard backed hard security action and the movement spawned from loyalist defence; it is inferred to resist accountability for forces.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Common Sense wants the state to address deprivation, unemployment and housing, which goes beyond a minimal state.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Beyond the Religious Divide envisages equal rights under a bill of rights and power-sharing with the Catholic minority.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not relevant to an anti-communist movement.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The movement treats Ulster as a legitimate national home of its people, not a colonial project.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: A bill of rights and common constitution implies equal civil law, though not stated for religious personal law.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The constitution would guarantee rights; no restriction is proposed.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Protestant cultural base likely defends religious instruction; not documented.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A socialist-state doctrine; the anti-communist Vanguard strand rejects its premise, so mild disagreement is inferred.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Common Sense requires a two-thirds referendum to adopt or amend the constitution and cites that status must not change without majority consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Trade balances are not discussed in the sources, so no stance is inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: Beyond the Religious Divide and Common Sense invite Catholic participation in a shared state.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The sources contain no theory of struggle as progress; Common Sense stresses agreement between communities instead.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Security-minded unionist politics has supported outlawing groups that attack the constitutional order, but Common Sense requires minorities to back the constitution and law and order.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Common Sense calls Westminster rule elected dictatorship, which echoes anti-arbitrariness, but no explicit doctrine.

separated-powers.rationale: Common Sense separates executive, legislature and a supreme court able to overrule the assembly.

vanguard-party.rationale: Not applicable; movement is a constitutional reform.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Common Sense lists deprivation and housing need as real enemies, but no priority principle is documented.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Right-leaning unionism would back it; not documented.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Barr and the Ulster Workers Council used strikes as the primary political tool in 1974.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Common Sense blames social deprivation and recession, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The movement sought to reconcile two communities but sources do not state a theory.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Common Sense uses election and proportional allocation by party.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Vanguard was hardline but Common Sense wants an entrenched bill of rights; split.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Barr's strike account shows concern for supplies of fuel and bread but not for price controls, so nothing is inferred.

party-controls-media.rationale: Common Sense invites open party competition and a bill of rights.

party-commands-army.rationale: Defence stays with Westminster and the state under the written constitution.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation is not discussed; the movement's focus is on Northern Ireland's existing communities.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Common Sense sets out assemblies and executives but not legislators' pay, so this stays neutral.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Common Sense wants party-based proportional politics, but nothing is said on binding members to party decisions.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Vanguard backed staying in the EEC and Common Sense accepts EEC advisers, but also wants own sovereignty.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The proposals use an assembly, executive and UK defence, not a head of state commanding forces.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not addressed; Protestant base is mostly Presbyterian.

clerical-rule.rationale: The proposals are a secular-form constitution with elected assembly.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Common Sense schedules elections every four years; no head-of-state view.

recall-officials.rationale: The proposal uses fixed four-year elections and does not mention recall, so no direction can be inferred.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Defence of NI relies on Westminster and its alliances.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Common Sense wants more housing, not abolishing rental.

people-in-arms.rationale: Loyalist paramilitary tradition vs UK defence reserved; split.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Not a theme in the sources; the loyalist base is mostly urban Belfast and rural Ulster Protestants, so adherents are split.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Barr says he would fight anybody to stay out of a united Ireland, and the movement is defined by rejecting one.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Barr's working-class loyalist perspective distrusts politicians more than graduates, so no clear inference.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The movement defends a particular culture.

death-penalty.rationale: Vanguard-era loyalism was hardline on terrorism; no explicit position.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Beyond the Religious Divide offers a state inclusive of Catholics, so descent-based citizenship is not inferred.

minority-language-support.rationale: The movement backs Ulster-Scots but is lukewarm about Irish; split.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Beyond the Religious Divide stresses equal rights and a bill of rights but says nothing on exemptions from general law.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Common Sense is about constitutional structure and does not take positions on social conformity.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not discussed; a state-building, property-respecting unionist outlook is inferred to favour repaying debts.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Independence is a constitutional aim, not an economic transformation.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Common Sense proposes an elected constitutional conference to draft the constitution.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Overseas aid is never mentioned in the sources, so no stance is inferred.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Defence is reserved to Westminster in the movement's plans, so a national deterrent question does not arise.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Common Sense proposes a US-modelled written constitution, as Beyond the Religious Divide did, but no sources state whether the head of state would be elected.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary institutions are never discussed in the sources, so the answer stays neutral.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Barr would fight to keep Northern Ireland out of a united Ireland, implying no territorial concession, though the case is about staying in rather than giving up land.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: No source gives a property doctrine, and the Protestant unionist base would be split.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: An anti-communist movement has no stake in this Marxist dispute; neutral.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental regulation is not covered in any source reviewed.

collective-defense.rationale: Defence is reserved to Westminster in Common Sense and Vanguard backed the western security order, so allied defence is inferred acceptable.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Protestant base is inferred to value church independence and the Orange Order's religious links, but nothing is documented.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Dominion proposals kept the Crown as a unifying head of state, so a symbolic nonpartisan head is inferred.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Adherents defend Northern Ireland's place in the UK by force if needed, but wish to separate from the UK themselves; split.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Common Sense wants Northern Ireland to keep its own devolved assembly and constitution within the UK, renegotiating the Act of Union.

sacred-ruler.rationale: The state proposed is a constitutional republic-like order with supreme court, not a sacred ruler.

character-from-environment.rationale: Not addressed; Common Sense blames deprivation for conflict, which leans environmental, but no doctrine.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Common Sense attacks unchecked parliamentary sovereignty as elected dictatorship and puts courts above the assembly.

space-expansion.rationale: Space policy is wholly outside the sources; neutral.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The model mixes coalition, courts and referenda, which is loosely mixed, but it is not framed that way.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family law is absent from the sources, so no stance can be inferred.

refugee-return.rationale: The movement says nothing on refugees or return rights; its own claim is to stay in Northern Ireland.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: The movement claims no territory beyond Northern Ireland, with Ulster-wide independence only in some versions; the UMSD wanted all nine counties, but this is minor.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: The Common Sense bill of rights rules this out.

women-must-cover.rationale: Inconsistent with bill of rights and Protestant culture.

common-currency.rationale: The independence aim implies own state; no currency view stated.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: The movement rejects uniting with Ireland and seeks separate state.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Common Sense proposes power-sharing among communities rather than separate cultural self-government.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The programme wants all in Northern Ireland, including Catholics, to play a full role in one society.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Marxist thesis rejected by anti-communist movement.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is not discussed in the sources, so nothing is inferred.

no-bailouts.rationale: Bailouts are not discussed in the sources, so this stays neutral.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Common Sense says a supreme court could overrule an assembly act that is unconstitutional and that no majority may rewrite the constitution without two-thirds.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Common Sense allocates posts by party strength, not gender.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The movement doubts Ulster could be self-sufficient and discusses viability with UK or Irish support.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Common Sense mentions EEC experts as advisers only; trade-agreement standards are not discussed.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The movement rejects revolution theory and treats force as defensive.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The Crown loyal and Orange tradition favours inherited institutions.

history-own-civilization.rationale: The movement values its own Ulster identity and Ulster-Scots heritage.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Common Sense insists on self-government by consent of the people concerned, so rule by a more advanced power is inferred to be rejected.

patriotic-education.rationale: Inferred from loyalist cultural emphasis on flag and heritage.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not a concern of the movement.

public-money-creation.rationale: Monetary system design is not mentioned in the sources, so no inference is made.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Right-leaning unionist base would say so.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The movement looks to the British Crown as link or Commonwealth realm, but does not seek influence over former empire regions.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Marxist thesis that an anti-communist, cross-class movement would not adopt; inferred from Vanguard's outlook.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Beyond the Religious Divide and Common Sense aim for equal rights and Catholic inclusion via a bill of rights.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Common Sense makes a bill of rights an essential part of the constitution, enforced by a supreme court and changeable only by referendum.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Not addressed; movement defends the existing partition.

elective-rulers.rationale: The proposal is elected assemblies and executive by PR.

minority-veto.rationale: Common Sense sets a two-thirds referendum and safeguards for minorities, not individual veto.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Craig said it would be Vanguard's duty if politicians failed and strike leaders resisted direct rule as undemocratic.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Common Sense calls parliamentary sovereignty an elected dictatorship and makes a supreme court able to overrule.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: No source discusses duties of the privileged; Common Sense stresses rights and shared responsibility among communities instead.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Barr and the loyalist leadership urged active participation, and Common Sense invites everyone to take part.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Hegemony theory is outside the sources, and the movement offers no account of how ruling groups maintain power.

native-born-offices.rationale: Common Sense reserves no offices by birth, but also does not address non-natives holding office.

party-own-road.rationale: A question internal to communist movements; Vanguard's anti-communism leaves no basis for an answer.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Debate on viability of independence: some doubt a state without UK or Irish support, so left split.

return-lost-territory.rationale: The movement seeks no lost territory.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The Ulster Protestant identity claims its own place and rejects hierarchy by descent.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Not addressed; Vanguard rejected fascist labels.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: The movement defends Orange marches and flags as heritage.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Gender-based policy attention is not addressed in the sources, so this stays neutral.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: The sources contain nothing on domestic violence policy, so no stance can be inferred.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: The movement wants a US-style constitution with bill of rights, but it does not argue about civilisational fit of institutions.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Defence is reserved to Westminster in the plan, and politics belong to elected institutions.

paid-care-work.rationale: Unpaid care work is never discussed in the sources.

filial-duty.rationale: Inferred from the movement's conservative Protestant cultural base; no document addresses family obligation.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Foreign ownership of firms is not discussed; Common Sense wants EEC and Commonwealth advisers, not isolation.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Not part of proposed fixed four-year terms.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Pension design is not discussed in any source.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Not part of unionist property outlook.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Common Sense wants a devolved elected assembly governing all but reserved matters, implying assembly control of budget.

single-official-language.rationale: The movement backs Ulster-Scots without making English sole in law; no view.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Land purchase by foreigners is not covered in the sources.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Common Sense relies on a bill of rights guaranteeing equal rights, not outcome-based tests, so mild disagreement is inferred.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Not discussed; Common Sense wants economic development, but adherents hold no documented view on consumption.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Vanguard's concern was defending Ulster against insurgents, so arming foreign ones is inferred to be rejected.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Common Sense insists on self-determination by consent and rejects imposition by outsiders, so imposed intervention is inferred to be rejected.

corporate-influence.rationale: Lobbying and campaign finance are not mentioned in the sources.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses foreign funding of NGOs, media or universities.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Population and family incentives are not discussed in the sources.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local limits on home purchases are not discussed in the sources.

job-guarantee.rationale: Common Sense names unemployment as an enemy, but no guarantee is proposed.

democratic-peace.rationale: International relations theory is outside the sources, so no inference is made.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Common Sense requires minorities to back law and order.

non-intervention.rationale: The sources do not address non-intervention, though Barr resents outside decisions taken behind people's backs.

industrial-unions.rationale: Barr's strike account involved shipyard and power-station workers but gives no view on union structure.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Common Sense seeks Catholic inclusion and fears of exclusion on both sides.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Common Sense wants written constitutional guarantees and openness of coalition government, so a mild lean to access rights is inferred.

local-production.rationale: Local food and goods production is not discussed in the sources.

informal-organisation.rationale: Formal parties and constitution are the proposal.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Common Sense wants Ulster constitution supreme, while accepting the European Convention.

religious-nation.rationale: The proposals aim at a non-sectarian state beyond the religious divide.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Barr rejected trusting English politicians and decisions made behind backs.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: The movement wants Ulster self-rule with financial self-interest; no explicit position.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Vanguard's right-wing, property-respecting stance implies personal belongings stay private, but this is inferred.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The sources do not discuss how public services are delivered.

religion-illusion.rationale: The movement is tied to Protestant religious identity and the Orange Order.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Inferred from Vanguard's right-wing, anti-communist outlook; no source gives a view on capitalism's historical role.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from Vanguard's right-wing outlook, which would not tie women's equality to economic transformation.

treaties-binding.rationale: Common Sense wants constitution changes by referendum, but does not address treaties between governments and nations within them.

majority-settlement.rationale: Both documents propose power-sharing with Catholics, not segregation.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The movement claims Ulster for its people but through settlement and residency, not historic tie.

holocaust-denial.rationale: No part of the programme supports denial; Common Sense aims at a bill of rights and equal participation for all groups.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred from a conservative Protestant base, though modern adherents have not made criminalisation a goal; not documented.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Common Sense includes a bill of rights and equal participation of all communities, which is inconsistent with state punishment of religious practice.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The movement wants Ulster governed by its own people for their benefit, so ruling territories for a metropole is inferred to be rejected.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: The programme is a secular constitutional scheme in which religious authority plays no role, so this doctrine is rejected.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Common Sense treats the problem as the two communities' constitutional exclusion, not overlapping oppressions; inferred disagreement.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred from a conservative Protestant cultural base; the sources do not discuss it.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Common Sense urges moving beyond the unionist-nationalist divide and Beyond the Religious Divide is similarly framed.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist notion that the anti-communist Vanguard strand would not endorse; inferred.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Islam is not a topic in the sources, and the movement's religious conflict is between Protestants and Catholics.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Authority comes from referendum and constitution, not God.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Not discussed; adherents are split between secular constitutional language and cultural attachment to religion.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Workplace harassment law is not mentioned in the sources.

social-market-economy.rationale: Common Sense joins economic development with social deprivation priorities.

rich-first.rationale: Common Sense proposes no development strategy of this kind.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Vanguard sided with the western bloc.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: A right-leaning, property-respecting unionist base is inferred to prefer ordinary banking, though nothing is stated.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The sources do not discuss lenders or austerity; Common Sense stresses employment and housing but names no funding source.

domination-women-nature.rationale: An ecofeminist claim outside the sources; mild disagreement is inferred from the movement's conservative base.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept that an anti-communist movement would not adopt; inferred disagreement.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Common Sense presents political rights as secured by constitution and referendum, not as hollowed out by wealth; inferred.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Written constitution, courts, rule of law.

online-participation.rationale: Online politics is not discussed; the sources date from the 1970s and 1980s.

open-government-data.rationale: Common Sense's open constitutional conference and referendum imply publicity of government, a mild inferred lean.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Beyond the Religious Divide aims for a state beyond sectarian division, with rights for the Catholic minority, which excludes limits on mixed marriage.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The 1979 proposals seek Catholic inclusion in a power-sharing state, so boycotts of a minority's shops cut against the programme.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Common Sense uses elected conference, not sortition.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Doctrinal reinterpretation is not a topic in the sources; Protestant adherents are divided between traditional and modern views.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Common Sense argues majority rule is undemocratic in divided societies and proposes proportional executive posts for all main parties.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Common Sense names deprivation as the enemy but sources say nothing on wealth and liberty; inferred as split.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: The culturally Protestant loyalist base is inferred to be socially conservative, in line with this audit's answer on same-sex marriage; no source states a position.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: A culturally Protestant movement defined against secular or Catholic absorption would oppose state unbelief; inferred from its Orange and Protestant identity.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Vanguard-era loyalism was hardline on security and Common Sense proposes a supreme court and rule of law; abolition is inferred to be rejected.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: The loyalist working-class base is attached to state services but also to church and community; sources are silent, so split.

term-limits.rationale: Common Sense proposes a written constitution and PR but says nothing on term limits.

vote-delegation.rationale: The programmes favour a written constitution, assembly elections and PR, i.e. representative institutions; delegable voting is inferred to be foreign to them.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Concerns were local constitutional and security questions; extinction risk as a policy priority is inferred to rank low.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: The Protestant cultural base includes conservative denominations that reserve offices to men; inferred, with no source on the point.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Sources say nothing on marriage; the Protestant base is mixed between traditional and egalitarian views.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Common Sense is silent on non-citizen voting; adherents' view is unknown.

rent-control.rationale: The sources do not address housing policy and the loyalist working-class base would be split.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed; the constitution-and-bill-of-rights programme in Common Sense is a liberal-democratic framework that would keep property rights.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Not stated; the UPRG's civic, power-sharing programme is inferred as not favouring drilled youth movements.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: The sources do not address nuclear weapons; adherents are not known to hold a view.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: The sources do not address basing; an independent or dominion Northern Ireland's defence arrangements are unstated.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; no inferable position.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Common Sense names deprivation and unemployment as the enemies, so a lean to rewarding work over ownership is inferred.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The UDA's research group came from a loyalist tradition of armed defence of the community, so an absolute ban is inferred as unlikely.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Ulster identity is tied to the Plantation-era settler community rather than ancient origins, so unbroken ancient continuity is inferred as rejected.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: A culturally Protestant, conservative community base makes social constructionism of sex inferred as rejected.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: The sources do not address feminist theory; adherents' view is unknown.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Loyalist commemoration of the dead exists, but Vanguard and Common Sense do not frame it as martyrdom; adherents are split.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: The sources do not frame politics as spiritual struggle; the evangelical Protestant base would be split.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not addressed; Ulster nationalism seeks a state for the province's own people rather than a diaspora centre.

culture-before-state.rationale: Its programmes put self-rule and a constitution first, so cultural renewal before state-building is inferred as rejected.

god-not-male.rationale: A conservative Protestant cultural base makes this inferred as disagreed, though not stated.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Same conservative Protestant base; the sources do not discuss feminist theology.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Common Sense proposes inclusive power-sharing with Catholics and a bill of rights, which rejects majority-group control of economic life.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Ulster nationalism seeks one self-governing Northern Ireland, but the sources do not say how a people's regions should be merged.

independent-unions.rationale: Not discussed; a bill of rights and civil-society safeguards in Common Sense suggest independent unions.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The sources focus on constitutional structure, not class power.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Common Sense names deprivation as the enemy; attachment of the loyalist base to the NHS suggests public hands for local essentials.

second-chamber.rationale: Common Sense proposes a single devolved assembly with proportional representation; a second chamber is not stated.

municipal-property.rationale: Not discussed; a devolved capitalist-mixed economy is assumed, not municipal ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The programmes seek a single Ulster-wide government, not a confederation of towns.

person-over-state.rationale: Common Sense's bill of rights and supreme court imply that individual rights limit what government may do.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Inferred from the culturally Protestant character of the movement, though the sources do not make spiritual nature a theme.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Its programmes want an entrenched written constitution because devolved Stormont was suspended by Westminster, so revocable powers are the thing it opposes.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The community defined is religious and national, not racial, and Common Sense stresses cross-community power-sharing.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred: pride in Ulster Protestant and Scots-Irish ancestry underlies the movement's identity, though the sources do not frame it as racial.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred: the movement wants an Ulster state defended against absorption, not wars of conquest; the loyalist paramilitary link complicates this.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The strand defined Ulster as its own people by history and Protestant culture, not by language, and rejected folding it into an Irish nation; inferred from its rejection of a united Ireland.

communal-electorates.rationale: Common Sense proposes proportional representation with posts shared among parties rather than separate religious rolls; inferred, since it never discusses communal electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Barr and Vanguard distrusted Britain and Dublin as ready to sell Ulster out; inferred from that distrust.

free-public-college.rationale: The sources never address tuition; nothing in the programmes points either way.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Environmental policy is absent from the sources and the strand had no stated position; left neutral.

future-generations.rationale: Never discussed; a mild yes inferred from the conservative, community-rooted outlook.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the strand's conservative, culturally Protestant loyalism that it would not give gender-based weight.

arms-reduction.rationale: Vanguard and the UDA were militantly anti-IRA and favoured strong security forces; inferred from that stance.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Never addressed; the sources give no basis for either side.

capital-controls.rationale: Anti-communist and pro-property with an open regional economy; inferred, as capital flows are not discussed.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred: the strand grew out of loyalist paramilitarism, such as the UDA's political wing, and treats community defence forces as legitimate until a settlement.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred from its loyalist-unionist roots, which stress duty to defend the community and the state.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred from its base in loyalist working-class and trade union action such as the Ulster Workers' Council strike.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Inferred from the pragmatic social policy in Common Sense, with support for working-class living standards.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Not addressed by its sources; adherents' economic views were pragmatic and mixed.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Inferred: the strand is focused on Northern Ireland's self-rule, not on global economic reform.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Common Sense seeks an agreed constitutional process and power-sharing, and Vanguard sought to use existing institutions, not smash them.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Inferred from its principle of community self-determination and a written constitution that lets Ulster arrange its own affairs.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred: nature as capital is not addressed in its sources and it has no ecological programme.

sacred-nation.rationale: Inferred: it treats Ulster's people as a distinct national community with a claim to self-rule, though it is more civic than sacred in the sources.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Inferred from its mildly social-democratic leaning in Common Sense; not addressed directly.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred: it holds that Westminster neglects and governs Ulster from outside, which parallels the centre-periphery grievance, though not in colonial terms.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Inferred from its socially conservative, Protestant-rooted outlook.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred: its documents accept established institutions and a bill of rights, and the UK's public broadcaster was not an issue for it.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Not addressed; the movement is culturally Protestant and Orange, so it is inferred to see the religions as not equivalent.

farm-price-support.rationale: Not addressed; its rural unionist base and loyalist working-class origins make support for protecting farmers a plausible inference.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Not addressed; Northern Ireland has no nuclear weapons of its own and sources are silent.

workers-own-party.rationale: Loyalist Vanguard and UDA groups competed with and worked alongside labour-aligned loyalist parties, and sources do not settle whether a separate workers' party was favoured.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not addressed; a civic bill of rights proposed in Common Sense suggests support for banning harmful practices, a weak inference.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Common Sense proposes a bill of rights with equal protection, so equal property rights for women are inferred.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not addressed; the movement stresses Ulster-Scots as a separate cultural heritage, which pulls toward distinct names, but evidence is thin.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Not addressed; sources are silent on environmental or tort law.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: The proposals favour a modern written constitution and elected bodies and make no mention of chiefs, which are foreign to Northern Ireland, so disagreement is inferred.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Not addressed; its liberal bill of rights proposals suggest it does not subordinate liberty, inferred.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Vanguard took a hard line on security and opposed the IRA, so fixed sentences for serious repeat offenders are inferred as supported.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Not addressed; Northern Ireland's main languages are English and Irish, and an Ulster identity that rejects the Irish language is offset by its pluralist programme.
